title: The Billionaire Raj's reckoning
gist: India's Gen Z 'Cockroach' protests forced the resignation of education minister Dharmendra Pradhan — a rare concession from Modi — but the author argues the real story is structural: 1m young Indians entering the labour market monthly, AI hollowing out the entry-level IT jobs that used to absorb graduates (Infosys shares down roughly a third in a year), and a worsening geopolitical position with China, Pakistan and a hostile Trump administration. Modi's political dominance is intact and a fourth term in 2029 looks likely, but the 'Billionaire Raj' of elite capture that the author named in 2018 has, on inequality, got worse rather than better.

themes.theme: Cockroach protests and the limits of the concession

insights.claim: India's education minister Dharmendra Pradhan resigned in late July 2026 after youth protesters led by activist Abhijeet Dipke's 'Cockroach Janta Party' filled central Delhi and a dozen other cities, a central demand of the movement.
insights.speaker: James Crabtree
insights.so_what: Ministerial scalps are a rare signal that Indian street pressure can still move policy — watch for further cabinet churn as a leading indicator of political risk premium on India assets.
insights.quote: A day earlier, education minister Dharmendra Pradhan resigned, fulfilling a central demand of the youth protesters who had thronged central Delhi and a dozen other cities.
insights.locator: Abhijeet Dipke appeared tired but content

insights.claim: The Cockroach demonstrations are the largest political protests in India since COVID and one of only a handful of sustained anti-government campaigns Narendra Modi has faced since taking power in 2014.
insights.speaker: James Crabtree
insights.so_what: Establishes a scale benchmark for Indian political unrest — useful for sizing whether future flare-ups are noise or regime-relevant.
insights.quote: The largest political protests since COVID, they are also one of only a handful of sustained anti-government campaigns Modi has faced since winning power in 2014.
insights.locator: As victory statements go, its modesty was apposite

insights.claim: A tech-savvy Gen Z movement of students and educated urban professionals forcing out one minister is not evidence of a broader legitimacy crisis, because that constituency is demographically unrepresentative of India at large.
insights.speaker: James Crabtree
insights.so_what: Do not extrapolate urban-elite protest imagery into a regime-change trade; Indian political continuity risk remains low.
insights.quote: A vocal, tech-savvy Gen Z campaign forcing out a minister is far from a broader crisis of legitimacy for the government as a whole.
insights.locator: The limits of that optimism should be obvious

insights.claim: The protest movement began as a joke when activist Abhijeet Dipke seized on India's Chief Justice comparing unemployed young people to 'cockroaches' in May, then escalated online before reaching the streets.
insights.speaker: James Crabtree
insights.so_what: Illustrates how low the ignition threshold now is for mass mobilisation in a smartphone-saturated youth economy — a recurring tail risk in emerging markets.
insights.quote: Dipke, a political activist, seized on the insult, launching the Cockroach Janta Party, basically as a joke.
insights.locator: The recent uprising traces back to the middle of May

insights.claim: Protest anger escalated in stages — from alleged corruption in cancelled national civil service and university entrance exams, to youth joblessness, and finally to rising inequality and weak government accountability.
insights.speaker: James Crabtree
insights.so_what: A grievance-escalation ladder worth tracking: exam/corruption scandals are the visible trigger, but jobs and inequality are the persistent fuel.
insights.quote: Along the way, the marchers’ complaints became broader still, encompassing unhappiness over rising inequality and weak government accountability.
insights.locator: Initial anger focused on allegations that corruption

themes.theme: Demographic overhang and AI hollowing out Indian IT

insights.claim: India has the world's largest youth population at 370 million, and per the World Bank one million young people enter its labour market every single month.
insights.speaker: James Crabtree
insights.so_what: The absorption maths is the core Indian macro constraint — any growth thesis that doesn't create ~12m jobs a year is politically unsustainable.
insights.quote: according to the World Bank, one million young people spill into the labour market each month
insights.locator: India’s underlying employment problem is getting worse

insights.claim: Artificial intelligence is hollowing out entry-level Indian IT work that once absorbed hundreds of thousands of educated graduates a year, removing one of the few reliable ladders into the middle class.
insights.speaker: James Crabtree
insights.so_what: The AI displacement story is not just a Western white-collar issue — it removes the demand-side pull for Indian IT services headcount and the political safety valve that came with it.
insights.quote: Artificial Intelligence is hollowing out entry-level IT work, which once absorbed hundreds of thousands of educated graduates a year.
insights.locator: Some avenues that once promised entry to the middle class

insights.claim: Shares in Infosys, a major Indian IT services company, have fallen by roughly a third over the past year, cited as market evidence of AI disruption to the services-outsourcing model.
insights.speaker: James Crabtree
insights.so_what: A concrete price signal linking AI adoption to the Indian IT services complex — the sector is being repriced as a disrupted incumbent rather than a growth compounder.
insights.quote: Shares in Infosys, a well known IT services company, have fallen by roughly a third over the past year.
insights.locator: Some avenues that once promised entry to the middle class

insights.claim: India's school and university systems remain deeply flawed and produce legions of underemployed graduates, so the country's education output is a source of frustration rather than of productivity.
insights.speaker: James Crabtree
insights.so_what: Human-capital quality, not quantity, is the binding constraint — bullish India demographic pitches should be discounted for skills mismatch.
insights.quote: School and university systems remain deeply flawed, leading to legions of underemployed graduates.
insights.locator: India’s underlying employment problem is getting worse

themes.theme: Geopolitical squeeze on India's growth model

insights.claim: Both of India's principal rivals, China and Pakistan, have become more threatening while ties with the United States, its most important partner, have worsened under President Donald Trump.
insights.speaker: James Crabtree
insights.so_what: India is losing its optionality of playing all sides — a deteriorating US relationship undermines the 'China+1' supply-chain reallocation trade.
insights.quote: Both of India’s principal rivals, China and Pakistan, have become more threatening. Ties with the US, its most important partner, have worsened under President Donald Trump.
insights.locator: None of this is made easier by a worsening geopolitical context

insights.claim: The war in Iran and the resulting inflation and energy costs caused enough economic hardship in India that Modi was forced to introduce a range of emergency fuel-saving measures.
insights.speaker: James Crabtree
insights.so_what: India remains a first-order loser from oil shocks; energy import dependence transmits Middle East conflict straight into Indian fiscal and political stress.
insights.quote: The war in Iran and associated rising inflation and energy costs caused economic hardship, forcing Modi to introduce a range of emergency measures to save fuel.
insights.locator: None of this is made easier by a worsening geopolitical context

insights.claim: Weakening economic globalisation itself undermines India's development strategy, because that strategy depends on exporting services and integrating into Western supply chains.
insights.speaker: James Crabtree
insights.so_what: India's growth model is levered to the very globalisation that is retreating — a structural headwind that compounds the AI hit to services exports.
insights.quote: Weakening economic globalisation in general makes it harder for India to grow by exporting services and integrating with Western supply chains.
insights.locator: None of this is made easier by a worsening geopolitical context

insights.claim: Narendra Modi is arguably India's most politically dominant leader since Jawaharlal Nehru, and only a brave pundit would bet against him winning a fourth term in 2029, equalling Nehru's record.
insights.speaker: James Crabtree
insights.so_what: Base case for India through 2029 is policy continuity under Modi — price political risk low but expect no structural break in the elite-capture problem.
insights.quote: Only a brave pundit would bet against him winning a fourth term in 2029, equalling Nehru’s record.
insights.locator: India is still led by its most powerful government in living memory

insights.claim: Modi's continued political dominance rests substantially on facing a divided and disorganised opposition rather than on solving India's structural problems.
insights.speaker: James Crabtree
insights.so_what: Electoral strength is a weak proxy for reform capacity — do not read BJP wins as evidence that jobs or inequality policy is improving.
insights.quote: So far, though, Modi appears impervious, not least given he faces a rabble of divided opposition parties.
insights.locator: India is still led by its most powerful government in living memory

insights.claim: The central paradox of Indian politics is that maximal political power coexists with minimal problem-solving capacity: Modi's grip is tightening even as youth unemployment, political fairness and state competence deteriorate.
insights.speaker: James Crabtree
insights.so_what: Strongman stability does not equal execution — the India long thesis should be underwritten on corporate earnings, not on assumed reform delivery.
insights.quote: For all his tightening hold on power, Modi is struggling to find answers to the new set of broader challenges India faces, from youth unemployment to political fairness and state competence.
insights.locator: The result is a conundrum

themes.theme: The Billionaire Raj thesis, a decade on

insights.claim: The term 'Billionaire Raj', coined in the author's 2018 book, describes how after India's 1991 liberalisation a new tycoon class accumulated vast fortunes through proximity to political power in Delhi, echoing the extractive British Raj and the bureaucratic Licence Raj.
insights.speaker: James Crabtree
insights.so_what: A durable lens for Indian equity analysis: conglomerate returns have historically been a function of political access, not just operating skill.
insights.quote: The term ‘Billionaire Raj’ captures how, in the decades after India’s 1991 liberalisation, a new and vibrant tycoon class worked with political friends in Delhi, accumulating vast fortunes through proximity to power.
insights.locator: In 2018, I published a book entitled The Billionaire Raj

insights.claim: Modi genuinely curtailed the worst freewheeling graft around India's cabinet table, but entrenched inequality and the power of the super-rich have if anything got worse — cleaning up corruption did not fix elite capture.
insights.speaker: James Crabtree
insights.so_what: Anti-corruption progress and distributional outcomes have decoupled in India — a warning against using governance-reform headlines as a proxy for social stability.
insights.quote: Meanwhile, the underlying issues of entrenched inequality and an ever-more powerful super-rich have, if anything, got worse.
insights.locator: To give Modi credit

insights.claim: The anti-corruption protests that helped bring Modi to power — Anna Hazare's India Against Corruption movement, with hunger strikes and sit-ins at Delhi's Jantar Mantar around 2011 — are now being replayed at the same site against him.
insights.speaker: James Crabtree
insights.so_what: Indian mass mobilisation runs in roughly decadal cycles around elite capture; the 2011 analogue suggests protest energy can eventually reshape the political map even when it looks contained.
insights.quote: There is a curious symmetry to all this, too, given it was a previous set of public protests that first helped propel Modi to power.
insights.locator: There is a curious symmetry to all this

insights.claim: The pre-Modi scandal wave that generated public fury spanned telecoms spectrum auctions and land allocations under a government seen as both corrupt and incompetent, which is what created the opening for a clean-up candidate.
insights.speaker: James Crabtree
insights.so_what: Sector-level graft scandals — spectrum, land — have historically been the trigger points for Indian regime change; watch resource-allocation scandals as political leading indicators.
insights.quote: There were huge scandals in areas from telecoms spectrum auctions to land allocations, under a government widely seen as both corrupt and incompetent.
insights.locator: Public anger back then focused on rampant graft

insights.claim: The enduring political risk in India is not regime instability but the persistence of a small elite capturing the gains of growth while the mass of younger Indians looks on.
insights.speaker: James Crabtree
insights.so_what: Frames the multi-decade Indian risk as distributional, implying rising odds of populist redistribution, tax or regulatory action against large domestic conglomerates.
insights.quote: the basic problem of a small elite capturing the gains of growth remains, while the mass of younger Indians look on
insights.locator: More to the point, the protests that once helped take him to power
